description: We are a team of three B.Tech students interested in software development, AI/ML, and solving real-world problems through technology. Our skills include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap, UI designing, and basic project development. We enjoy learning new things, sharing ideas, and working collaboratively. We are looking for teammates with skills in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, or web development who are enthusiastic and willing to contribute and learn together.
summary:
Mission Atlas is a web-based educational platform developed to showcase the history and significance of space exploration equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. It provides an interactive way to explore historical, ongoing, and upcoming space missions through a mission archive, 3D Orbital Graveyard, ISS 3D exploration, Deep Space Signal Delay Simulator, and Then and Now visualisations. Additional features include an interactive planetary landing-site map, knowledge-based quizzes, and an AI-powered assistant.

The project addresses the challenge by presenting complex space mission histories, spacecraft information, and scientific achievements in an accessible, engaging, and visually interactive format. It helps school-age students and casual space enthusiasts understand the purpose, contributions, and legacy of these machines. The platform is important because it preserves the stories of past space missions, encourages interest in space science, and connects historical discoveries with future exploration.
details:
1. Project Overview and Functionality

  • Mission Atlas is an interactive, web-based educational platform that brings the stories of forgotten space exploration equipment on the Moon, Mars, and beyond back to life.
  • It features a Mission Archive, 3D Orbital Graveyard, ISS 3D Exploration, Deep Space Signal Delay Simulator, Then and Now visualisations, interactive planetary maps, educational quizzes, and an AI-powered assistant.
  • Users can explore mission histories, spacecraft locations, scientific contributions, and the legacy of past explorations.

2. Key Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes complex space science and mission histories easier and more engaging to understand.
  • Encourages interactive learning through 3D visualisations, simulations, maps, and quizzes.
  • Inspires school-age students and space enthusiasts to explore astronomy, space technology, and scientific discoveries.
  • Connects past space missions with present achievements and future exploration.

3. Technology and Development Tools

  • Developed as a web-based prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Combines interactive web development, visualisation, simulation, and AI-powered features.
  • Designed to be accessible through a web browser without requiring specialised hardware.

4. Creativity and Innovation

  • Focuses on forgotten and abandoned space equipment rather than only active space missions.
  • Introduces creative features such as the 3D Orbital Graveyard and Deep Space Signal Delay Simulator.
  • Uses interactive storytelling and historical comparisons to turn mission data into an exploratory learning experience.
  • Combines educational content with modern web technologies to create a more immersive experience.

5. Key Development Considerations

  • Factual accuracy and reliability of space mission information.
  • Educational value and suitability for school-age audiences.
  • User-friendly navigation and accessibility.
  • Visual appeal and interactive engagement.
  • Technical feasibility and effective integration of different features.
